name: From Katana to Camcorder: Japan's Road to Power
description: Emperors, warlords and shoguns, a country that closed its doors, opened them, built an empire, fell in war and rebuilt itself on trains, cars and electronics.

checkpoints.name: Court and warriors
checkpoints.note: Shinto shrines honour the gods, and from 794 the Imperial House rules from the Heian court in Kyoto. In the provinces a class of mounted warriors, the samurai, armed with swords and bows, slowly gains power.

checkpoints.name: Rule of the warrior
checkpoints.note: Shoguns ruled in place of emperors, and samurai drove back the Mongol invasions of 1274 and 1281. Swordsmiths perfected the katana, the long curved blade that became the samurai's mark.

checkpoints.name: The country at war
checkpoints.note: In the Sengoku period lords fought each other. Oda Nobunaga broke his rivals, Toyotomi Hideyoshi united the country and invaded Korea, and Tokugawa Ieyasu won the Battle of Sekigahara in 1600.

checkpoints.name: Peace under the Tokugawa
checkpoints.note: The Tokugawa shogunate kept the peace for two and a half centuries and closed Japan. Himeji Castle was finished and Edo, now Tokyo, grew into one of the world's largest cities, until Perry's ships arrived in 1853 and the Treaty of Kanagawa opened Japanese ports.

checkpoints.name: Meiji, empire and war
checkpoints.note: The Meiji Restoration brought a new constitution and fast industrial growth. Japan beat China in 1895 and Russia at Tsushima in 1905 and ruled Korea from 1910, and Toyota began making cars in 1937. Under Hirohito the Empire of Japan went to war and was defeated after Pearl Harbor, Midway and the atomic bombs.

checkpoints.name: Japan rebuilt
checkpoints.note: Post-war Japan rebuilt on electronics, cars and trains: Sony, the Honda Super Cub, the Shinkansen opened for the 1964 Tokyo Olympics, the Walkman and Japanese camcorders, until the asset bubble burst around 1991. In 2011 the Tohoku earthquake and tsunami struck the north-east.
